newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve accords with Caucasian republics.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve accords with Caucasian republics.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday approved a series of planned agreements between the European Union and four former Soviet republics.
Euro-MPs had to give their assent to the partnership agreements with Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, before they could become law.
The accords cover a wide range of aspects, including political cooperation, trade, environmental protection, cross-border provision of services, regional cooperation and nuclear safety.
They also provide for cooperation to be suspended in the case of grave violations of human rights.

Hans van den Broek, the EU commissioner for relations with central and eastern Europe, told the parliament the agreements were important for the EU because the former Soviet republics were major suppliers of products ranging from energy sources, minerals, metals and chemicals.
They were also important markets for EU products, the commissioner said.
